chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah al-Saghir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah was when there was nothing that was. Then He created existence and place, and created the Light of lights by which the lights were illuminated, and caused to flow within it from His Light by which the lights were illuminated. And that is the light from which He created Muhammad and Ali. They remained two first lights when nothing had been brought into being before them. Then they continued to pass on, pure and purified, through the pure loins until they were separated in the purest of two pure ones: in Abdullah and Abu Talib عليه السلام.

key_terms.عَلِيًّا: Ali عليه السلام, created from that light
key_terms.مُحَمَّدًا: Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, created from that light
key_terms.نُورَ الْأَنْوَارِ: the Light of lights, the primordial light-source of illumination
key_terms.نُورَيْنِ: two lights, referring to their primordial luminous reality
key_terms.نُورِهِ: His Light, from which illumination proceeds

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the primordial light of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Allah’s pre-eternal existence and speaks of the creation of a primordial light from which Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Ali عليه السلام were created. It emphasizes their purity, primacy, and transmission through pure lineages until their separation in Abdullah and Abu Talib عليه السلام.
